assumptions.stall: 2.2 kg·cm / 0.8 A at 6 V (official); 5 V not specified

arm_drive.note: Worst case is the arm horizontal. paw_force_at_stall = 2.2 kg·cm at r=71 mm (blade centre) — the most a blade can push on a finger before the servo stalls.

clasp_grip.mechanism: Both FS90MG arm servos drive their forearm blades toward each other about the shared shoulder axis; the object is squeezed between the blades.
clasp_grip.compliance: 2 mm fur sleeve over each blade (≈4 mm of compressible pile in the clasp). Squeeze is set by commanding the blades past contact; the servo's position loop then pushes up to stall. No spring or breakaway part.
clasp_grip.note: Datasheet stall torque 2.2 kg·cm at 6 V, both servos at stall; 5 V torque is not specified (expect less). Not measured. Holding a stalled FS90MG continuously heats it: grip at ≤50 % for long holds, and let the INA219 trip limit current.

arm_reach.note: Torso front is y=-40, head front ≈ y=-37. Negative y = in front of the bear. The desk is z=0 (torso bottom).

arm_travel.interlock: armL - armR >= 7.5 deg (left blade over right)
arm_travel.pulse_map: ≈ 500–2500 µs over 180° (FS90MG spec); calibrate centre per servo; ≈0.85° of differential angle per mm of grip gap

head_pan.servo: FS90MG in the yaw collar (unchanged from v3)
head_pan.note: Yaw axis is vertical, so gravity does not load the pan servo; friction on the 0.35 mm journal is untested.

pinch_gaps_mm.note: The clasp is a deliberate pinch point: the blades close to ~1 mm and can trap a finger with up to ~3 N per the datasheet torque. Hub/shell rigid gaps are under 4 mm. Not assessed against any toy standard.

shoulder_pod_vs_fur_envelope.note: Positive = the printed pod corner pokes outside the nominal 4 mm torso fur envelope (fur skin must be patterned over it).

servo_power.note: Budget the 5 V servo rail for ≥2.4 A peak or stagger moves in firmware. The XL6009 module is not specified for that; the protected 2 A+ Pololu S13V20F5 is closer but still below an all-stalled peak.
